title: DTCR retrieval result
description: The rows one bounded query returned, each carrying an exact back reference and the authority it will keep for the rest of the task. Every row is a SEMANTIC_ROW and a NON_AUTHORITATIVE_CANDIDATE by construction: a stored row is not a ledger event and does not become one by being cited beside one, and a row that arrives ranked first arrives as a suggestion that a document may be relevant rather than as a finding that it is correct, current or binding. A result recorded as NOT_APPLICABLE carries no rows and states why, which is where the manufactured lane is refused: rows cannot be produced for a lane that was never entered. Rows carry a score and the method that produced it, because a similarity number without its metric is a figure that survives every later change to the index it came from.

row_class.description: A stored row is not a ledger event. The two live in different stores with different truths, and a row relabelled as an event inherits an authority the store never had.

authority.description: The same constant the violation candidate's semantic items carry, so a row keeps its ceiling when it is cited there.

back_reference_ref.description: The exact source behind the row. An orphan row is the mutation this field refuses: retrieval returns it, a reader reads it, and nothing says where it came from.

then.description: No synthetic vector lane. A plane that could not help this task returns no rows and says why; rows attached to it are manufactured to complete a picture.
A result announcing rows and carrying none is an empty result wearing a fuller headline.

rows.score_method: cosine similarity over the projection recorded in DTCR-PR-001, reranked by keyword overlap

examples.not_applicable_rationale: this task is a mechanical rename with no decision, incident or objective that stored context could bear on
